transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Cascade - Head of Security), Liam O'Rourke (Cascade - Platform Lead), Sara Kim (Cascade - Compliance), Derek Huang (Cascade - Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Cascade Utilities evaluating hybrid BYO-HSM + Redwood private deployment. Main concerns: key custody, rotation, cross-region residency, SSO/RBAC mapping, audit logs and proof for SOC2/ISO audits. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share compliance artifacts, SE to send HSM connector details, schedule PoC for envelope encryption and access policies.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for time. we'll run through how redwood supports BYO keys and hardware modules, and then dive into your access patterns.
[00:00:12] Maya Patel: Thanks, Avery. Quick note, I'm Maya — we run security for Cascade. We want to understand where keys live, who can touch them, and what proofs we get for audits. Sock two and ISO are our primary laundry list.
[00:00:25] Diego Morales: great, and hi all. i'll try to cover the HSM connector and envelope flow — there might be a little detail in the diagram i send after.
[00:00:35] Liam O'Rourke: Our environment is hybrid — some services in GCP, some on prem. We need BYOK so keys never leave our custody and we need to see latency impact on inference.
[00:00:45] Avery Chen: Totally. two main models: full BYO-KMS with HSM in your environment (we call this private-key routing), or hosted-master-keys with customer-wrapping keys. Both support envelope encryption.
[00:00:56] Sara Kim: small clarification, when you say HSM connector — is that a daemon we run in our VPC? Or a managed connector from Redwood?
[00:01:05] Diego Morales: It's lightweight. we have a connector you deploy in your VPC (container or VM) that speaks to your HSM/TAPs using KMIP or cloud vendor APIs — we support PKCS11 and KMIP adapters. we do not persist raw key material in Redwood — we keep only encrypted key refs.
[00:01:23] Derek Huang: you said KMIP and PKCS11 — our HSM is a Thales module and also a TPM fleet for edge devices, could that work?
[00:01:31] Diego Morales: yes, Thales is supported via KMIP. TPM for edge is trickier — you can provision ephemeral wrapping keys in the TPM and then have envelope keys stored in your HSM; we'll sketch the pattern in the diagram.
[00:01:43] Maya Patel: For audits we need key rotation records, split duties for key admins, and immutable audit logs with retention of 7 years. How do you produce those?
[00:01:53] Avery Chen: We emit audit events at token and key operation granularity. For Private deployments the audit streams can be pushed into your SIEM via syslog or secure HTTPS ingestion. We also provide signed log bundles for snapshots to support forensic review.
[00:02:06] Liam O'Rourke: Are those signed? We need tamper evidence.
[00:02:10] Diego Morales: Yes, logs can be signed with a separate log-signing key. For HSM-backed setups, log-signing can be done inside the HSM and Redwood will surface the signature metadata in the bundle.
[00:02:21] Sara Kim: what about separation of duties? We want operators to be prevented from rotating keys without approval.
[00:02:27] Avery Chen: RBAC is fine-grained — roles map to SAML attributes. You can enforce approvals via workflow hooks. In Private we integrate with your SSO (SAML/OIDC) and map groups to roles: key-admin, key-approver, key-operator, service-account. Approvals can require 2 approvers for rotation if you want.
[00:02:42] Maya Patel: nice. Does Redwood store any key material? You said encrypted references, but are there any cases where plaintext crosses Redwood boundary?
[00:02:51] Diego Morales: no plaintext. with BYOK/HSM, the private key never leaves your HSM. Envelope encryption flow: Redwood receives plaintext payload, but we usually recommend that customers perform client-side encryption or use the connector to do local wrapping before sending payloads. For model KV cache we keep only ciphertext and KID references.
[00:03:09] Derek Huang: latency — if wrapping/unwrapping happens in our HSM on-prem, will inference latency increase? our p95 token path is tight.
[00:03:18] Avery Chen: Good question. best practice: use envelope keys with a short-lived data key cached in the serving layer. the HSM is only hit on rotation or when cache miss. Redwood's runtime has a KV cache for data keys; we can pin pre-warmed keys so per-token path doesn't call the HSM. so steady-state latency impact is minimal.
[00:03:38] Liam O'Rourke: so roughly, HSM calls are once every N minutes on rotation or cache evictions — do you have suggestions for TTLs?
[00:03:45] Diego Morales: We usually see 5-15 minute TTLs for data keys depending on memory and risk appetite. for low-latency we push toward 15m and a conservative refresh strategy.
[00:03:55] Maya Patel: cross-border residency — some keys must not leave EU. We run HSM in our EU region. How do we ensure no accidental replication?
[00:04:02] Avery Chen: For Private deployments, you control where connectors run and where keys live. Redwood's control plane can be regionalized; we support regional tenancy so metadata and encrypted refs can be restricted. We'll include region guardrails in the rollout plan.
[00:04:15] Sara Kim: any legal concerns around key escrow? Our compliance team is nervous about third-party escrow.
[00:04:20] Diego Morales: we offer options: no escrow, customer-managed escrow, or escrow to a neutral vault with locked policies. for SOC2/ISO you just need documented policy and access controls. we'll note what Cascade prefers.
[00:04:33] Liam O'Rourke: for SSO mapping, what attributes do you need? We have complex groups and nested roles.
[00:04:38] Avery Chen: SAML groups and an attribute for role id are typical. Diego, maybe call out the minimal attribute set?
[00:04:44] Diego Morales: minimal: subject (email), groups, and a role-claim (optional). we recommend a dedicated SAML application so you can control assertion lifetime.
[00:04:53] Derek Huang: would like to test it end-to-end in a staging VPC before production. Can you provide terraform modules or helm charts for the connector?
[00:05:00] Diego Morales: yes, we'll share terraform + helm. the connector runs as a Deployment, and we also have a lightweight sidecar option for strict network policies.
[00:05:09] Maya Patel: how do you handle key compromise scenarios? Is there a playbook?
[00:05:13] Avery Chen: we have a compromise runbook. steps: revoke compromised key, rotate envelopes, invalidate caches, notify affected routes, rotate master-wrapping key in HSM, and provide signed audit of operations. we can run a tabletop with your incident response team.
[00:05:27] Sara Kim: good — we need to see the runbook and a sample rotation timeline.
[00:05:31] Avery Chen: we'll include that in the artifacts.
[00:05:35] Liam O'Rourke: what's the onboarding timeline for Private with BYO-HSM? from kickoff to pilot?
[00:05:40] Diego Morales: typically 3-6 weeks: week 1 requirements and network setup, week 2 connector and PoC, weeks 3-4 pilot load testing, week 5 production cutover depending on org gating.
[00:05:51] Maya Patel: cost question — does locking keys in our HSM add operational cost in Redwood billing?
[00:05:56] Avery Chen: there is a small connector maintenance fee and egress for hosted control plane operations; for Dedicated/private we include options with flat monthly charges for the connector and premium SLA. we'll surface numbers in the pricing doc.
[00:06:07] Derek Huang: routing — if Redwood loses access to our HSM regionally, what's fallback?
[00:06:12] Diego Morales: you can configure fallback policies: route to a compatible regional HSM or to a lower-cost hosted variant with customer consent. automatic fallback is opt-in; we also support manual failover. All failovers are logged and auditable.
[00:06:26] Sara Kim: for SOC2 we need continuous monitoring evidence. Does Redwood provide monitoring dashboards of key usage?
[00:06:32] Avery Chen: yes, Redwood Console shows per-key metrics, request origin, client id, success/failure rates, and anomalies. We can export dashboards or provide read-only views to your auditors.
[00:06:45] Liam O'Rourke: Are there known limitations — like model KV cache size affecting key rotation frequency or some corner cases?
[00:06:52] Diego Morales: large KV caches increase memory, which is why we recommend tuning TTLs. also if you have very small HSM throughput, you may need to add an intermediary key distribution tier to avoid throttling. we'll do benchmarks in your environment during PoC.
[00:07:05] Maya Patel: Any clients using a mix of on-prem HSM and cloud KMS in production? We want references for that pattern.
[00:07:11] Avery Chen: yes, we've done hybrid setups for a utility customer that kept master keys on-prem and used cloud KMS for edge workloads with careful guardrails — we can share an anonymized case study.
[00:07:22] Derek Huang: ok let's talk about data flows briefly — when a request hits Redwood runtime in our VPC, is there any plaintext at rest on Redwood nodes?
[00:07:30] Diego Morales: plaintext is only in memory during inference. we do not persist plaintext to disk. all writes go out encrypted, and ephemeral caches are in-memory with process isolation. for extra caution you can enable encrypted runtime RAM and secure enclaves in certain deployments.
[00:07:48] Sara Kim: What about backups for the key store metadata? Is that encrypted and region-bound?
[00:07:54] Avery Chen: metadata backups are encrypted with a backup key, and we can keep them in-region only. snapshots are signed and we can support long term retention policies.
[00:08:04] Liam O'Rourke: Okay so next practical steps?
[00:08:07] Avery Chen: We'll: 1) share SOC2 and ISO artifacts, 2) send the HSM connector spec + terraform, 3) provision a sandbox Private environment and invite your SSO for RBAC testing, 4) run a 2-hour PoC to validate envelope key flow and latency.
[00:08:20] Maya Patel: sounds good. also please include the sample legal template for BYOK language so legal can review.
[00:08:26] Avery Chen: will do.
[00:08:29] Diego Morales: I'll also attach a short bench script and sample results from a similar hybrid customer so you can see numbers.
[00:08:36] Derek Huang: Great. thanks everyone.
[00:08:39] Maya Patel: thank you.

(opaque seconds of wrap-up and scheduling)
[00:09:30] Avery Chen: I'll send meeting notes and calendar invites for the PoC slot we tentatively held for next Tuesday.
[00:09:40] Close remarks and goodbyes.

End transcript.
